title: Growth and Characterization of Irradiated Organoids from Mammary Glands
protocol: Sacrifice athymic Nu/Nu mice using CO₂ asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation.
Clean the skin using 70% ethanol.
Resect abdominal and inguinal mammary glands from mice using pre-sterilized scissors and forceps.
Remove lymph nodes before resection.
Rinse mammary glands in sterile 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Place the mammary glands in 15 mL tubes with 10 mL of Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Media/Nutrient Mixture F12 (DMEM/F12) for transport.
Irradiate samples at 20 Gy using a cesium source.
After 45 min of irradiation, place the mammary glands in a 35 mm sterile cell plate and mince with scalpels.
Mince the tissue with approximately 40 strokes until pieces are no larger than approximately 1 mm² in area.
Transfer minced tissue to the collagenase solution in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Collagenase solution consists of 2 mg/mL collagenase, 2 mg/mL trypsin, 5% v/v fetal bovine serum (FBS), 5 μg/mL insulin, and 50 μg/mL gentamicin in DMEM/F12 media.
Use 10 mL collagenase solution per mouse.
Place in a water bath at 37 °C, vortexing every 10 minutes for 30-60 minutes.
Spin down the digested solution at 450 x g for 10 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Precoat all pipettes, pipette tips, and centrifuge tubes with BSA solution prior to use.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh BSA-coated 15 mL tube.
Pipette up and down vigorously to disperse the fat layer.
Centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at RT.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving a small amount of media in the tube to avoid aspirating the cell pellet.
Aspirate the aqueous layer from the tube with the original pellet.
Add 10 mL of DMEM/F12 to the tube containing the original pellet and transfer it to the second tube.
Pipette vigorously to combine and resuspend the two pellets.
Centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at RT.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 4 mL of DMEM/F12 to the tube.
Add 40 μL of DNase solution (4 U/mL in DMEM/F12) to the suspension.
Gently shake by hand for 2-5 min at room temperature.
Add 6 mL of DMEM/F12 and pipette thoroughly.
Centrifuge the tube at 450 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant to the 0.5 mL mark.
Resuspend in 10 mL of DMEM/F12 and pipette thoroughly.
Pulse to 450 x g and stop 4 s after reaching that speed.
Repeat steps 1.16-1.17 three more times to purify organoids via centrifugal differentiation.
Resuspend pellet in 10 mL of DMEM/F12.
Pipette thoroughly to create a homogenous solution.
Transfer 50 µL to a 30 mm Petri dish and view under a phase contrast microscope at 20x.
Count the number of organoids with a tally counter.
Calculate the organoid density using an appropriate equation.
Centrifuge samples at 450 x g for 5 min if the density is too low.
Aspirate media and add necessary media to reach 1,000 organoids/mL.
Pipette thoroughly to create a homogenous mixture of organoids in media.
Seed organoids at a concentration of 1 organoid/μL in collagen type 1 diluted to 87% or basement membrane extract for growth.
Keep samples on ice while working with them.
Transfer the desired volume of organoids to a separate centrifuge tube for freezing.
Spin down the tube at 450 x g for 5 min and aspirate media.
Add an equal volume of 90% FBS/10% DMSO to resuspend the organoids.
Aliquot into cryotubes and store in -80°C, then transfer to liquid nitrogen within one week.
Thaw frozen organoids by warming them in a 37°C water bath for one minute.
Centrifuge at 450 x g for 5 min after thawing and aspirate freezing media.
Rinse the organoids with sterile DPBS and centrifuge again.
Aspirate DPBS and add organoid media to the resuspended organoids.
Pipette 50 µL (50 organoids) into each well of the low adhesion plate.
Add 150 µL of organoid media to bring the total working volume to 200 µL.
Every 2 days replace media carefully by aspirating slowly and adding new media slowly to avoid shear forces on organoids.
Maintain GFP or dTomato-labelled RAW 264.7 macrophages in DMEM media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Seed 1 x 10^4, 5 x 10^4, or 1 x 10^5 cells/mL into organoid media for co-culturing with macrophages.
Monitor macrophage infiltration over time using live cell phase contrast and fluorescent imaging.
Gently pipette up and down until organoids have detached from plates to transfer them.
Transfer detached organoids to chamber slides and incubate for 4-8 h to allow adherence.
Remove organoid medium from the wells carefully by aspirating slowly.
Fix samples with 10% neutral buffered formalin for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 minutes each in 1x PBS.
Store fixed samples at 4°C for up to one week if desired.
Permeabilize samples with 0.1% 4-(1,1,3,3-tetramethylbutyl) phenyl-polyethylene glycol for 5 minutes.
Stain samples with phalloidin diluted 1:1,000 and 1.67 nM bisbenzimide nuclear dye in 1% PBS/BSA for 1 hour at room temperature if staining for F-actin.
Proceed to step 4.8 after staining with phalloidin and nuclear dye.
Permeabilize samples with 0.5% PBS.
Block samples with 5% normal goat serum in 0.1% PBS/Polyethylene glycol sorbitan monolaurate (PBST) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 minutes each in PBS.
Incubate samples with Anti-Cytokeratin 14 diluted 1:1,000, E-Cadherin diluted 1:200, or Tight Junction Protein One diluted 1:100 in 1% NGS in PBST for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 minutes each in PBST.
Incubate samples with Goat Anti-Rabbit secondary antibody diluted 1:200 in 1% NGS/PBST for 1 hour at room temperature, covered with foil to avoid light exposure.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 minutes each in PBS.
Stain nuclei using the nuclear dye from Table of Materials.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 minutes each in PBS.
Mount chamber slide samples with a coverslip if applicable.
Store slides wrapped in foil at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
